title: Scheme-theoretic fibre of a morphism over a point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and let $s\in S$ be a point, with residue field $\kappa(s)$ and canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ (the morphism induced by $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\kappa(s)$, with image $s$). The *scheme-theoretic fibre* of $f$ over $s$, or simply the *fibre* $X_s$, is the fibre product $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ with its projections $X_s\to X$ and $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$; it is regarded as a scheme over $\kappa(s)$ through the second projection. The first projection is a homeomorphism from the underlying space of $X_s$ onto the subspace $f^{-1}(s)$ of $X$.
